prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your needs (budget, timeline, system type, warranties, etc.). A quick way to get the right company is to compare 3–4 qualified contractors using the checklist below. Before I recommend specific companies I can’t verify in real time, tell me your ZIP code and a bit about the job (single-family home or condo, central AC or heat pump, approximate age of system, target budget/timeline) and I’ll help you narrow it down and draft questions/requests for bids.

Quick checklist: what a top HVAC contractor should provide
- Proper licensing and insurance: verify Georgia registration and current liability insurance/workers’ comp.
- NATE-certified technicians (or equivalent training).
- A Manual J load calculation (not a rule-of-thumb) to size the replacement correctly.
- Matched equipment (indoor coil and outdoor unit) and refrigerant type clearly specified.
- Written, itemized estimate that shows equipment make/model, SEER rating, line-set/new ductwork needs, permit and inspection fees, labor warranty, parts warranty, and any change-order policy.
- Permit pull and code-compliant installation.
- Clear timeline for work, removal/disposal of old equipment, and final testing/commissioning.
- References and strong recent online reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB).
- Financing options and available energy-efficiency rebates (local utility/Georgia programs).
- Post-installation support: a walkthrough, documentation, and a contact for callbacks.

Questions to ask every contractor (phone or on-site)
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?
- Do you perform a Manual J load calculation for system sizing?
- What specific brand and model are you proposing? What is the SEER/HSPF?
- What warranties come with the equipment and the labor? Are warranties transferable?
- Will you handle permits and inspections?
- Who will do the work — your employees or subcontractors? Are they NATE-certified?
- What is the total out-the-door price and what’s included (thermostat, condensate pump, duct modifications, permit)?
- Can you provide recent references from homes in my neighborhood?
- What is the projected start and completion date?
- How do you handle post-install callbacks and service?

Red flags
- No written estimate or refusal to run a Manual J.
- Pushy sales tactics, high-pressure “today only” discounts.
- Very low bids without clear scope — likely to add change orders.
- No proof of insurance or license.
- Poor or no recent reviews and no references.

How to compare bids (apples-to-apples)
- Make sure each quote uses the same: equipment model (or equivalent SEER), coil pairing, refrigerant, and ductwork scope.
- Check included labor warranty length and what is excluded.
- Check if the contractor will start only after permit approval and pays for the inspection.
- Ask for a list of included services (thermostat wiring, startup, refrigerant charge, duct sealing).

If you want, I can:
- Draft a script/email you can send to contractors.
- Create a comparison checklist template to evaluate quotes side-by-side.
- Suggest several Atlanta-area contractors (I’ll just need your ZIP code so I can give targeted, commonly well-rated options).

Which would you like me to do next?
